title: Choose Code Duel's visual world
question: The roll assigned Tournament Hall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tournament Hall
options.lineage: school chess club: roll-up vinyl boards, the two-faced clock, the carbon scoresheet
options.thesis: Every round is a rated game: a clock with a flag, a scoresheet, and annotation marks on every move.
materials: black clock case with a red flag
options.viewport: Game screen: problem left, editor right, a header clock in a black case whose red flag lifts in the last 30 s, and a scoresheet strip notating each question (1. BH-E01 !! +148).
options.risk: Annotation marks (!!, ?!) lean on chess literacy; each needs a plain-words tooltip and legend or new players read noise.

raised.raise: Clock, score and room-code numerals are built on one condensed numeral system, so they read across a desk at a glance.
Every neutral snaps to a nine-step board-green ramp; no off-ramp greys anywhere.
Each scoring rule is printed beside its live number (Run tests 3 · −5%), never as a paragraph.
The question browser and topic picker reveal detail only on the focused row, so lists stay scannable.

options.label: Timing Tower
options.thesis: Code Race as a race: a live timing tower of gaps, with splits coloured fastest, personal best, or slower.
options.viewport: Game screen with a right-edge timing tower: players stacked by score with +gap intervals, each question a split tile in purple, green or yellow.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of 'Code Race' and close to the dark-screen-plus-neon look; strong but expected.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Numbers are the game: timer, score and room code built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Game screen on a pale ground with a faint grid; the timer and score are huge grid-built numerals in the header band; 3-2-1 countdown assembles cell by cell.
options.case: Holds product clarity (huge numerals read instantly, no chess knowledge needed); loses audience identification (Dutch modernist posters are not students' world).
options.risk: Pale ground for 60-minute night sessions, and the grid must stay out of the problem text.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every question as a catalog number on matte black, topics as colour codes.
options.viewport: Question ids as the only headlines; topic decoded on hover.
options.case: Loses both: codes instead of words hurt beginners, and the reference is foreign to students.
options.risk: Coded labels hide meaning from learners.
options.kept: The question id (BH-E01) treated as the one catalogue headline, never labelled twice.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over a zone ramp, hatching as state.
options.viewport: Sliding sheets over an eleven-step tonal field.
options.case: Loses both: darkroom craft means nothing to the audience and hatching obscures test state.
options.kept: A single fixed tonal ramp as the only neutral tokens.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: One neutral scale, one accent, every claim beside its proof.
options.case: Loses both: reads as a SaaS tool, not a game, against a game-first brief.
options.kept: Every rule paired with its live proof number.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Questions as poster tiles in category rows.
options.viewport: Rows of question tiles by topic.
options.case: Loses both: questions have no artwork to carry tiles, and the game screen gains nothing.
options.kept: Metadata revealed only on the focused item.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Fixed-scale plates following one subject through stages.
options.case: Loses both: soft, bookish, and nothing to do with competition.
options.kept: Per-question results compared on one fixed shared scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A competitive-programming site executed impeccably: dark IDE shell, one accent, difficulty tags.
canonCard.viewport: Problem tab left, editor right, a toolbar with Run and Submit, a results drawer below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every practice site by design.
